headline: 2 token contracts catalogued from audit page (Pharos chain); no on-chain reads performed; Sui and Bitcoin chain addresses not discovered; GitHub not pinned.

findings.text: D1: Protocol.chains lists Bitcoin and Sui. Bitcoin has no smart-contract explorer for EVM-style address lookup. Sui explorer search was not attempted (no Sui addresses surfaced from other sources). Pharos (Pacific) is the actual deployment chain for the BTCvp vault token per docs, but is not listed in protocol.chains — no Pharos block-explorer search attempted. Zero addresses surfaced from block-explorer name-tag search.

D2: docs.vishwalab.com is the canonical docs site (confirmed via llms.txt and vault pages). No standalone 'Deployed contracts' page was found in the docs index; contract addresses were only discovered via the Audits & Compliance page at docs.vishwalab.com/security/audits-and-compliance.md. deployed_contracts_doc set to null (no dedicated page found).

D3: The Audits & Compliance page (fetched via .md endpoint) lists three FuzzLand audits dated 08/20/2025 covering token contracts, BTC ZK-circuits, and light client; one FuzzLand Agent Product audit delivered 10 June 2026; and one ExVul audit (June 2026) covering BTCvp (0x79D154287DDC77e5C10127E68c2df1a942a330BB) and Cfvc (0xa3b81AA35A2462c588639483EBe68a856Cb32b0d) from vishwanetwork/lightclient-verifier at a pinned commit. Report PDFs are stored at GitBook file links that are not directly fetchable. Chain for these contracts is unlabelled in the audit text — vault overview says 'Pharos (Pacific)' not Sui.

D4: No GitHub URL is pinned in protocol.github. The audit text references repos vishwanetwork/veta-server, vishwanetwork/vishwa-cli, vishwanetwork/agent-api, and vishwanetwork/lightclient-verifier, all under a 'vishwanetwork' GitHub org — but no commit SHA was surfaced in fetchable text and no direct GitHub URL was fetched. Cannot record commit-addressed artifacts.

D5: Bitcoin: no smart-contract addresses to enumerate (UTXO chain). Sui: zero addresses surfaced from any corpus. Pharos (Pacific): BTCvp and Cfvc addresses surfaced from audit page. Chain identity mismatch — protocol.chains says Bitcoin/Sui but the live product runs on Pharos.
D6: No factory addresses surfaced from any corpus. Not applicable at this stage.

D7: BTCvp (0x79D154287DDC77e5C10127E68c2df1a942a330BB) classified as token (proof-of-asset receipt token). Cfvc (0xa3b81AA35A2462c588639483EBe68a856Cb32b0d) classified as token (unspecified, co-listed with BTCvp in ExVul audit scope). Chain is Pharos (not Sui or Bitcoin). Actor class unknown — bytecode not read.
D8: Both addresses trace directly to the fetched docs.vishwalab.com/security/audits-and-compliance.md page. No snippet-only sightings without fetch backing.

rationale.verdict: Discovery run walked the protocol website, two docs domains (docs.vishwanetwork.xyz and docs.vishwalab.com), the vault overview, risk/governance, and audits/compliance pages. Two token contract addresses were catalogued from the ExVul audit scope entry. No GitHub repo, no dedicated deployments page, and no Sui or Bitcoin on-chain addresses were discovered. Chain identity mismatch (protocol.chains=Bitcoin/Sui vs. live deployment on Pharos) leaves the address book incomplete. grade=unknown because no on-chain reads were performed and the discovered addresses' chain (Pharos) has no supported chainId in the DeFiPunkd read API, precluding surfacer-URL generation.

protocol_metadata.about: Vishwa is banking infrastructure for autonomous capital, enabling AI agents and institutions to hold, move, and grow digital assets through pre-execution enforcement controls. Every agent request is authorized against configurable policy limits (spend caps, venue allowlists, AML/sanctions checks), moved via a unified API across payment rails and stablecoins, and attested on-chain via ERC-8150 signed proofs. The flagship product is the Naro BTCvp Vault, a guardrailed BTC yield vault on Pharos where native BTC is held in custody with Ceffu, BTCvp receipt tokens are minted 1:1, and yield is generated through market-neutral strategies verified by the Veta execution layer before each capital movement. Vishwa is non-custodial by design — the control layer enforces policy before execution but never holds customer funds or private keys.
